title: Employment Situation, March 2027 (BLS, 08:30 ET) — the first payroll after the March SEP meeting, and the last untracked one before jobs-2027-05-07
source: EST: derived from BLS's own scheduling rule — release on the third Friday following the end of the reference week, the Sun-Sat week containing the 12th. The rule was re-implemented from scratch by the never-assessed research of jobs-2027-01-08 on 2026-09-09 and validated against BLS PRIMARIES rather than against sibling ledgers: 102 of 106 primary-dated reference months reproduce exactly, from BLS's own historical release-date table (bls.gov/bls/histreleasedates.pdf, 1957-2000, parsed deterministically) and its current schedule page (bls.gov/schedule/news_release/empsit.htm, fetched 2026-09-09, covering Nov 2025 through Nov 2026); the four disagreements are the 1995-96 and 2025 shutdown displacements plus one unexplained 1998-11-05 pull-forward. March 2027's 12th is a FRIDAY, so the reference week is Sun 2027-03-07 to Sat 2027-03-13 and the third Friday after 03-13 is 2027-04-02. NEITHER DOCUMENTED CORRECTION APPLIES: not a December reference month, and 2027-04-02 is not a federal holiday. It is, however, GOOD FRIDAY — 2027's Easter falls on 2027-03-28, so Good Friday is 2027-03-26 and this date is clear of it; that was checked rather than assumed, because a Good Friday collision would close the NYSE while BLS stayed open and would need its own handling. Prefix is EST: and not BLS: because bls.gov has published no 2027 schedule at all — /schedule/news_release/2027_sched.htm returned HTTP 404 on 2026-09-09 — and a derived date is not a published one. Discovered in the never-assessed initial research of jobs-2027-01-08, 2026-09-09
notes: PROPOSED, NOT CANONICAL. Filed with its sibling jobs-2027-03-05.from-jobs-2027-01-08.json to close the last of a measured GAP: canonical jobs-* entries jump from 2026-12-04 to 2027-05-07, leaving January through April 2027 untracked. With jobs-2027-01-08 canonical as of this PR and jobs-2027-02-05 already proposed by the treasury-refunding-2027-02-03 lane (deliberately not re-proposed here — a competing proposal buys nothing and the scanner warns on it), this file closes the hole. WHY IT IS WORTH TRACKING: from federalreserve.gov's own 2027 calendar (HTTP 200, page-stated 'Last Update: August 19, 2026'), the March 16-17 meeting carries a Summary of Economic Projections; this is the FIRST labour print after it and the last one before the already-tracked jobs-2027-05-07. HONEST LIMITS: the date is derived, not published, and the derivation's own validation set is 1993-2000 plus 2025-11..2026-08 — the 2001-2024 stretch is reproduced by the corrected rule but was not primary-checked month by month. April is also the one release month where a first-Friday payroll can collide with Good Friday, and any lane researching this id should re-derive the Easter date rather than inherit it. Re-check once bls.gov publishes a 2027 schedule. Note for sibling lanes: bls.gov returns HTTP 403 to curl from this runner on every route, but SERVES the same pages to WebFetch, which is how the schedule page, the historical release-date PDF and individual archive releases were retrieved on 2026-09-09. symbols: [] and status estimate: nothing here licenses an entry.
